name: Rice Stem Borer
description: Caterpillar pests that bore into rice stems, causing dead heart, white heads, and reduced yield. They are among the most damaging pests of rice in Africa and Asia.
symptoms: Dead heart (central leaf whorl drying) in vegetative stage
White heads (empty panicles) at reproductive stage
Small entry holes near stem base
Frass and stem tunneling visible when stem is split
Egg masses (covered with brown hairs) on leaf tips
treatments: Apply granular insecticides (carbofuran) into floodwater at early infestation
Use neem-based botanical insecticides as preventive spray
Spray chlorantraniliprole for effective larval control
Crush egg masses by hand where visible
prevention: Plant early to escape peak borer populations
Keep fields clean of alternate weed hosts
Flood fields deeply during egg-laying periods
Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest
references: Africa Rice Center Stem Borer Management
